questions.text: What kind of device is a transformer?
answers: A device that increases or decreases an alternating voltage.
A device that produces electromagnetic oscillations.
A device that detects radioactive radiation.

questions.text: Find the expression for the transformation ratio of a transformer.
The primary coil of a transformer has 800 turns and the secondary coil has 3200 turns. Determine the transformation ratio.
A voltage of 220 V is applied to the primary coil of a transformer. If the transformation ratio is 0.8, what is the voltage across the secondary coil (V)?
A voltage of 220 V is applied to the primary coil of a transformer. The primary coil has 400 turns and the secondary coil has 200 turns. What is the voltage across the secondary coil (V)?
The secondary coil of a transformer has 990 turns, the input voltage is 220 V and the output voltage is 330 V. How many turns does the primary coil have?
The primary coil of a transformer has 40 turns. How many turns must the secondary coil have in order to raise the voltage from 220 V to 22000 V?
In the interconnected ideal transformers shown below, $N_1/N_2 = 8$ and $N_3/N_4 = 1/3$. What is the output voltage $U_2$ (V)?
In the secondary circuit of a step-down transformer the voltage is 80 V and the current is 2 A. What is the current in the primary coil (in amperes) if the voltage across it is 160 V? Neglect losses.
In this transformer the input power is $P_1 = 100$ W and the output power is $P_2 = 80$ W. If $U_1/U_2 = 10$, what is the ratio $I_2/I_1$?
A step-down transformer with an efficiency of 90 % draws 2600 W of power from the mains. Determine the power of the current in the secondary coil (kW).
The voltage across the primary coil of a transformer is 200 V and the current is 0.5 A; in the secondary coil they are 38 V and 2.5 A. What is the efficiency of the transformer (in percent)?

In the transformer shown in the figure the efficiency is 75 %, the rms current in the primary coil is $I_1 = 1$ A and the rms voltage is $U_1 = 200$ V. Determine the rms current through the resistance $R = 6\ \Omega$ in the secondary coil (A).

The output voltage of a step-down transformer is 30 V. 100 light bulbs, each drawing a current of 0.8 A, are connected to it. If the efficiency of the transformer is 96 %, what is its input power (kW)?
When power is transmitted from a generator of 60 kW at a voltage of 2400 V, the voltage drop in the line must not exceed 10 %. What is the maximum allowed resistance of the wires ($\Omega$)?

Electric power of 100 kW is to be transmitted at a voltage of 10 kV through a copper wire with a cross-sectional area of $17\text{ mm}^2$. What is the maximum distance over which it can be transmitted so that the energy loss does not exceed 5 % (km)? $\rho = 1.7 \cdot 10^{-8}\ \Omega\cdot\text{m}$.
How does the amount of heat released in the transmission wires change if the voltage in the power transmission system is increased by a factor of 2?
answers: It increases by a factor of 4.
It decreases by a factor of 4.
It increases by a factor of 2.

questions.text: When the voltage was raised without changing the power of the current source, the energy loss in the transmission wires decreased by a factor of 100. By what factor was the voltage increased?

Which of the following waves is longitudinal?
1) waves on the surface of water; 2) sound waves in liquids and gases; 3) electromagnetic waves; 4) waves arising in the strings of musical instruments.
Under what conditions are electromagnetic waves radiated?
answers: when an electron moves uniformly in a straight line.
when an electron moves uniformly in a straight line in a conductor.
when a neutral atom moves with acceleration.

questions.text: Charge 1 moves uniformly in a straight line; charge 2 moves in a straight line with acceleration; charge 3 performs harmonic oscillations; charge 4 moves uniformly along a circle. Which of these charges radiate electromagnetic waves?
What type of wave are electromagnetic waves?
How is the direction of propagation of an electromagnetic wave determined? (The direction of propagation of the electromagnetic wave is the same as the direction of motion of a corkscrew)
answers: when the handle of the corkscrew is turned from $\vec{E}$ to $\vec{B}$.
when the handle of the corkscrew is turned from $\vec{B}$ to $\vec{E}$.
when the handle of the corkscrew is turned clockwise from $\vec{E}$.
when the handle of the corkscrew is turned counterclockwise from $\vec{E}$.

questions.text: How are the directions of the vectors $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ of an electromagnetic wave propagating from a source related to the vector $\vec{v}$ indicating the direction of propagation?
The vectors $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ of an electromagnetic wave in vacuum point along the X and Y axes. What is the direction of propagation of the wave?
answers: In the positive direction of the X axis.
In the positive direction of the Y axis.
In the negative direction of the X axis.
In the positive direction of the Z axis.

questions.text: The speed of propagation of electromagnetic waves in vacuum...
answers: is equal to their speed in a medium.
is less than their speed in a medium.
is greater than their speed in a medium.
is zero, because they do not propagate in vacuum at all.

questions.text: The distance between the 1st and 4th maxima of an electromagnetic wave is 30 m. What is the wavelength of this wave (m)?
Find the relation between the frequency $\nu$, the speed $v$ and the wavelength $\lambda$ of an electromagnetic wave.
What is the propagation speed of an electromagnetic wave with a frequency of $8\cdot 10^{14}$ Hz and a wavelength of 200 nm (m/s)?
What is the wavelength of an electromagnetic wave with a frequency of 10 MHz emitted from a spacecraft (m)?
If the frequency of an electromagnetic wave in vacuum is $3\cdot 10^{13}$ Hz, what is its wavelength (m)?
Find the distance shown in the figure for an electromagnetic wave with a frequency of $8\cdot 10^{14}$ Hz and a propagation speed of $1.6\cdot 10^8$ m/s (nm).
A "cell" phone operates at a frequency of 100 MHz. What is its operating wavelength (m)?
An electromagnetic wave passed from a medium with a dielectric constant $\varepsilon=2$ into vacuum. How does the distance it travels during a time equal to one oscillation period change?

Give the expression for the speed of an electromagnetic wave propagating in a medium with dielectric constant $\varepsilon$ and magnetic permeability $\mu$. The speed in vacuum is c; $\lambda_0$ and $\lambda$ are the wavelengths in vacuum and in the medium, respectively.
The intensity of an electromagnetic wave is...
answers: the electromagnetic energy W per unit volume.
the ratio of the electromagnetic energy W passing through an area $\Delta S$ in a time $\Delta t$ to the product $\Delta S \Delta t$.
the ratio of the electromagnetic energy W passing through an area $\Delta S$ to the quantity $\Delta S$.
the ratio of the electromagnetic energy W to the time interval $\Delta t$.

questions.text: The intensity of the electromagnetic radiation of a point source is...
answers: directly proportional to the distance from the source.
inversely proportional to the distance from the source.
proportional to the square of the distance from the source.
inversely proportional to the square of the distance from the source.

questions.text: When moving along the direction of radiation from the first point to the second by 6 m, the radiation intensity decreased by a factor of 4. How far from the radiation source is the first point (m)?
Taking the distance to the Earth as $150\cdot 10^6$ km, find the total radiation power of the Sun (kW).
How does the power radiated by an open oscillating circuit change if the frequency of the electromagnetic oscillations is increased by a factor of 2?

If the frequency of the electromagnetic wave radiated by a vibrator increases by a factor of 3, by what factor does the wave energy radiated per unit time increase? Assume the wave amplitude is constant.
The current in the oscillating circuit of a radio receiver varies as $i = 10^{-6}\sin10^6\pi t$ (A). To what frequency (Hz) is it tuned?
The charge on the capacitor of a receiver's oscillating circuit varies as $q = 2 \cdot 10^{-9}\sin5 \cdot 10^5\pi t$ (C). What is the wavelength of the received wave (m)?
The charge on the capacitor of a radio receiver circuit varies as $q = 10^{-9}\cos4 \cdot 10^4\pi t$ (C). To what frequency (Hz) is the receiver tuned?
How must the capacitance of the capacitor in the oscillating circuit of a radio receiver be changed to increase its receiving frequency by a factor of 2?
A radio transmitter installed on a spacecraft operates at a frequency of 20 MHz. What is the wavelength of the radio wave it emits (m)?
An antenna radiates an electromagnetic wave with a frequency of 6 MHz. How many waves fit over a distance of 100 km in the direction of propagation?
A radio wave with a frequency of 5 MHz is generated in a circuit. How many wavelengths fit over a distance of 150 km in the direction of propagation?
Determine the frequency of a radio wave with a wavelength of 10 cm (Hz).
The capacitance of the capacitor in the oscillating circuit of a radio receiver is 1000 pF and the inductance of the coil is 1 mH. To what wavelength (m) is it tuned?
The inductance of the oscillating circuit of a radio receiver corresponding to a wavelength of 300 m is 2.5 mH. What is the capacitance of the capacitor in the circuit (pF)? $\pi^2\approx 10$.
The inductance of an oscillating circuit tuned to a radio wave of wavelength 1884 m is 2 mH. What is the capacitance of the capacitor in it (pF)?
The capacitance of the capacitor in an oscillating circuit tuned to a wavelength of 1884 m is 500 pF. What is the inductance of the coil in it (mH)?
The wavelength of the radiated electromagnetic waves is $1.2\cdot 10^8$ m. What is the law of variation of the current in the radio antenna?
If a signal sent by a radar returned after 420 $\mu$s, what is the distance to the object (km)?
A radar emits 1000 pulses per second. What is the maximum distance at which it can observe an object (km)?
A radar sends 2000 pulses per second. Find the maximum range of the radar (km).
